newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar inaugurates giant Rasgas LNG plant.
newsitem.headline: Qatar inaugurates giant Rasgas LNG plant.

text.p: Qatar's Crown Prince Sheikh Jassim bin Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani on Monday laid the foundation stone of the Gulf Arab state's second liquefied natural gas (LNG) plant.
Ras Laffan Liquefied Natural Gas Company (Rasgas) is one of Qatar's three multibillion-dollar gas export projects to tap reserves in North Field, the world's largest single concentration of gas.
Qatari Minister of Energy and Industry Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah, speaking at the ceremony, described the project as an avenue for Qatar to secure a leading role in the international LNG market.
"This will enhance Qatar's position as a major gas producing country and will open the way for Qatar to have a leading role in international LNG," said al-Attiyah.
"In fact, Qatar has all of what it takes to play this leading role, based on the enormous gas reserves in the North Field," he added.
Rasgas has signed an agreement to export 4.8 million tonnes of gas annually for 25 years to Seoul's Korea Gas Corporation (Kogas) from mid-1999.

The company is 63 percent owned by the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation, 25 percent by U.S.-based Mobil Corp, four percent by Itochu Corp, three percent by Nissho and five percent by an undisclosed South Korean entity designated by Kogas.
Rasgas said in a statement that 2,500 people are currently working at the project and the drilling of wells in the North Field began last month. The number of workers is expected to exceed 6,000.
